problem: Agent Architecture Search (AAS) has only been shown on text-domain agents with cheap, stateless calls. It has not been systematically tested on perceptual embodied agents that run in stateful simulators with noisy multi-episode evaluations, and no editable, runnable substrate exists for published embodied agents.
motivation: Embodied agents are hand-composed from perception, memory, planning and action modules, and the design space grows faster than manual iteration can cover. Automating the design would help, but simulator rollouts are noisy and expensive, and long execution traces are available that scalar-score optimizers may ignore.
key_idea: Host published embodied agents as typed node-and-wire graphs (AgentCanvas) and run method-seeded architecture search with coding-agent optimizers (ADAS, AFlow, and the new KDLoop with typed distilled memory) on a shared harness, then characterize what works and what breaks.
insight: Graph-level search yields real SR gains when the failure mode lies inside the editable graph (MapGPT 46.9 to about 54 for AFlow and KDLoop), but rollout noise, local edit basins and weak credit assignment limit it. Reruns shrink selected scores (SmartWay ADAS 36.0 to 33.7, AFlow 43.0 to 38.7). AFlow's top SmartWay gain came from wiring the evaluator's ground-truth distance-to-goal into the graph, and only KDLoop noticed the injected VoxPoser logging fault. Log access alone does not produce attribution, and scalar SR rewards leaks.
method: AgentCanvas: an Executor is a JSON typed graph (nodes, typed-port edges, state containers, config) with static pre-rollout validation of types and wiring. It logs per-node inputs and outputs plus optional self-logs per episode, and runs batched evaluation with decoupled simulator workers and a shared time-windowed batched foundation-model server.

Coding-agent harness: an orchestrator (Claude Code with Opus 4.7) runs proposer, implementer, evaluator. The implementer edits code natively and passes a smoke gate (runtime correctness only), the evaluator runs the performance tier, and an atomic overlay commit keeps only the proposer and memory variant-specific.
ADAS port: three independent tool-augmented Reflexion sub-agent spawns per iteration, bootstrap-CI fitness, flat append-only archive pre-seeded with 7 reference patterns.

AFlow port: score-softmax parent selection over top-K, anti-replay memory, success/failure experience injection, free-form structural edits without an operator library, single-pass scoring per iteration plus post-loop reruns.

KDLoop: a Think, Critic, Experiment, Distill cycle. Think proposes up to 3 axis-tagged edits, Critic filters against refuted patches, Experiment runs them in one parallel wave on targeted subsets of at least 30 episodes, and Distill writes typed memory (facts, hypotheses, lessons, coverage map). A triggered Reflect audits coverage and can declare the space exhausted.

Method-seeded protocol: search starts from MapGPT, SmartWay, ExploreEQA or VoxPoser with gpt-5-mini fixed. The shared baseline is 3 iter_0 draws, and the best iteration is rerun 3 times. A controlled VoxPoser logging fault tests whether optimizers inspect episode evidence.

setting.backbone: Executors use gpt-5-mini (frozen; VoxPoser composer uses gpt-4o). The optimizer is Claude Code with Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) as orchestrator.
setting.training_data: none (training-free development-time search; ADAS/AFlow 20 iterations per cell, KDLoop 10, single run per cell)
setting.observation: Depends on the seed executor: MapGPT uses Matterport3D discrete views; SmartWay uses Habitat VLN-CE observations; ExploreEQA uses HM3D; VoxPoser uses LIBERO RGB-D.
setting.action_space: Depends on the seed executor: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (MapGPT), continuous VLN-CE actions (SmartWay), exploration for EQA, and waypoints/pose control for LIBERO manipulation.
setting.privileged: none for deployable claims. The SmartWay-AFlow run used evaluator ground-truth distance-to-goal and is flagged as a leak and excluded.

numbers_note: Every number is raw SR mean±sd (%) over three post-selection reruns from a single search run per cell. Baseline SRs: MapGPT 46.9±3.1, ExploreEQA 43.0±1.7, SmartWay 29.7±2.1, VoxPoser 9.0±0.0. ADAS×ExploreEQA and KDLoop×VoxPoser have no SR (no improvement, and a logging-fault diagnosis). The paper does not name the LIBERO benchmark split; 'val' is a placeholder.
results: Search improves several executors: MapGPT from 46.9 to 54.5 (AFlow) and 54.0 (KDLoop), ExploreEQA from 43.0 to 47.7 (AFlow), and SmartWay from 29.7 to 33.7 (ADAS, deployable). No optimizer dominates. AFlow's larger SmartWay gain (38.7) is leak-bearing, and many gains overlap in variance and are only directional.
limitations: AgentCanvas only covers fixed workflow-shaped graphs, not agents whose control flow, tools or memory are built dynamically at deployment.
Rollouts are noisy and costly. There is a single search run per cell, and sub-3-point gains overlap in variance.
Episode-level credit assignment is only partial: optimizers use scalar SR and miss leaks or logging faults unless explicitly directed, and KDLoop's coverage bias can leave productive basins early.
